# Bitcoin Solo Miner Monitor

> Self-hosted dashboard, REST API and MCP server for compatible AxeOS and cgminer-API Bitcoin miners. Readings and controls depend on firmware. It discovers miners on the LAN, monitors hashrate, temperature, power and shares, connects to the user's own Bitcoin node and solo pool (Public Pool, ckpool), estimates block odds, sends alerts, and lets an agent control miners within safe limits. Version 1.1.2.

This server: http://YOUR-SERVER:8420
Everything below is also available as JSON at http://YOUR-SERVER:8420/api/v1/agent/guide.

## Before setup or upgrade

- Read https://github.com/smokeysrh/bitcoin-solo-miner-monitor/blob/main/AGENTS.md and choose the official platform artifact from https://github.com/smokeysrh/bitcoin-solo-miner-monitor/releases/latest: Windows installer, GitHub release wheel for pipx, or the GHCR image for Docker. Use the release wheel URL rather than a bare PyPI package name.
- Before an upgrade, back up the app database and preserve its encryption key, data directory or Docker volume, settings and miner configuration. Legacy v0.9.x migrate-legacy imports miner hosts, ports and names; preserve the old data for historical telemetry.
- After launch, read this running server's /llms.txt or /api/v1/agent/guide. Check /api/v1/meta, set authentication for the network before sharing access, and use the least scope needed. Start with monitoring only.
- Preserve existing settings. Ask only for missing RPC credentials, electricity price or alert preferences. Have the user enter secrets through secure app fields; keep passwords, tokens, RPC credentials and wallet addresses out of chat and logs.
- For CLI preflight, bsmm discover --cidr 192.168.1.0/24 --json scans without adopting; substitute the user's private range. Show candidates and wait for confirmation. bsmm setup --yes scans again and can adopt all new miners and connect a discovered Public Pool without asking. Use it only after approval of that behavior and range; for specific-device approval use the API flow below. --yes skips the password prompt, so arrange authentication first. Setup output may contain an admin token: protect it and use a read token after setup.

## Set it up for a user

1. Learn what this server is and how far setup has got: `GET /api/v1/meta`
   No login needed. Look at auth.mode and setup.*
2. Get a token (only if auth.mode is 'password'): `POST /api/v1/auth/tokens` with body `{"name":"my agent","scope":"admin"}`
   For setup only: needs an admin session or an existing admin token. On the server itself you can run: bsmm token create --name setup --scope admin. For monitoring use --scope read instead. Protect token output; never paste it into chat or logs.
3. Find the user's miners: `POST /api/v1/discovery` with body `{}`
   Returns a job id. Poll GET /api/v1/discovery/{id} until status is 'finished' (about 20 s). Only private networks are scanned. If the server runs in Docker bridge mode pass the user's LAN, e.g. {"cidrs": ["192.168.1.0/24"]}.
4. Start monitoring what was found: `POST /api/v1/discovery/{id}/adopt` with body `{}`
   Show the miner and node/pool candidates and wait for confirmation before adopting. An empty body adds every new non-duplicate miner; pass keys containing only approved host:port values to select miners. Add one approved miner by hand with POST /api/v1/devices {"host": "192.168.1.50"}.
5. Connect the user's Bitcoin node or solo pool (optional but recommended): `POST /api/v1/sources` with body `{"kind":"public_pool","url":"http://umbrel.local:2019"}`
   The discovery result lists likely candidates under 'sources'. kinds: bitcoin_core (needs rpc_user/rpc_password in 'secret'), public_pool, ckpool, mempool_space. Connect only the approved source. Ask for missing node credentials through secure app fields; never guess or expose them in chat.
6. Set the electricity price so costs are right: `PATCH /api/v1/settings` with body `{"energy":{"price_per_kwh":0.12}}`
   Example only: preserve an existing tariff or ask for the missing price. Currency units are the user's local currency.
7. Set up an alert channel: `POST /api/v1/notifications/channels` with body `{"kind":"ntfy","name":"Phone","config":{"topic":"pick-a-secret-topic"}}`
   Preserve existing channels or ask which destination the user wants. GET /api/v1/notifications/channel-types lists every kind and its fields. After agreement, POST /api/v1/notifications/channels/{id}/test.
8. Protect the dashboard (recommended if others share the network): `POST /api/v1/auth/password` with body `{"new_password":"<enter securely>"}`
   Do this before exposing the server to an untrusted network. Preserve existing authentication; enter the password through secure app fields. Use a read-scoped token for monitoring after setup.
9. Verify: `GET /api/v1/overview`
   One call with fleet totals, odds, network, alerts, events. Also check the dashboard, GET /api/v1/health and GET /api/v1/system/diagnostics. Return the dashboard URL and a plain-English report; identify anything unavailable.

## Authentication

- Read http://YOUR-SERVER:8420/api/v1/meta first (no login). If `auth.mode` is `none`, no credentials are needed.
- Otherwise send the token in the `Authorization` header with the `Bearer` scheme. Scopes: `read` < `control` < `admin`.
- On the machine running the app: `bsmm token create --name agent --scope read` prints a token once. Protect that output. Setup may need admin access temporarily; routine monitoring uses read.

## Common tasks

- How are my miners doing? -> GET /api/v1/overview, then GET /api/v1/devices
- What are my odds of finding a block? -> GET /api/v1/odds (add ?hashrate_ths=50 for a what-if)
- What is my chance in the next 10 minutes? -> GET /api/v1/odds: horizons.ten_minutes (seconds=600), also in bsmm odds and MCP get_odds. This is a fixed-window Poisson chance of at least one block, not the chance of winning the very next network block. Bitcoin targets 10-minute blocks; the exact future block time is unknown. Past work never makes a miner due.
- Is anything wrong? -> GET /api/v1/alerts/active and GET /api/v1/insights
- Restart a miner -> POST /api/v1/devices/{id}/actions/restart (needs 'control' scope)
- Point miners at my own pool/node -> POST /api/v1/devices/actions {"action":"set_pool","all":true,"params":{...}} previews by default; send dry_run=false to apply
- History / charts -> GET /api/v1/fleet/history?range=24h&metrics=hashrate_hs,power_w
- Live updates -> GET /api/v1/stream?topics=device,event,fleet (Server-Sent Events)
- Prometheus / Grafana -> GET /metrics
- Report a bug -> Attach the output of GET /api/v1/system/diagnostics to a GitHub issue

## Safety rules for agents

- Ask before hardware controls, restarts, pool or payout changes, tuning, firmware changes, deleting data or other destructive actions. Confirm the target; read payout changes back through a private confirmation view.
- Control actions are audited and can be switched off in Settings > Safety (allow_control). Frequency/voltage changes are OFF until the user enables allow_tuning.
- Bulk actions preview by default (dry_run: true). Show the user the preview before sending dry_run=false.
- Secrets (RPC passwords, bot tokens, webhook URLs) are write-only: they are never returned by any endpoint.
- Do not guess node credentials, wallet addresses or passwords. Ask for missing information through secure app fields; keep secrets and addresses out of chat and logs.
- Network scans are limited to private address ranges.
- Restarting a miner interrupts hashing; downtime depends on firmware. Lost hashing time reduces the chance of finding a block.
- Solo mining is a lottery. Never promise a block or profit or say the user is due. When available, horizons.ten_minutes (Next 10 minutes) estimates chance over a fixed 600-second window; the next network block can arrive at any time.

## Conventions

- Field names carry units: `hashrate_hs` (H/s), `power_w`, `temp_asic_c`, `efficiency_j_th`.
- Errors are always `{"error": {"code", "message", "hint", "status"}}`.
- Bulk miner actions preview with `dry_run: true`; check the endpoint schema before assuming another operation supports a preview.
- Live updates: `GET http://YOUR-SERVER:8420/api/v1/stream?topics=device,fleet,event` (Server-Sent Events).
